headline: Baqai Dental College students strengthen preventive dentistry skills through fluoride training
snippet: KARACHI: Strengthening preventive dentistry requires dental students to understand not only how oral diseases are treated, but also how evidence-based interventions can help prevent them. A Fluoride Gel Application Workshop at Baqai Dental College provided students with academic instruction and practical exposure to topical fluoride therapy, highlighting the role of fluoride in dental caries prevention and community oral healthcare. Organised by the Department of Community Dentistry, Baqai Dental College, the workshop focused on the scientific basis, indications and clinical application of fluoride gel as a professional preventive measure. Connecting dental education with preventive care The workshop was conducted under the guidance and supervision of Prof Dr Asghar Ali Shigri, Head of the Department of Community Dentistry, Baqai Dental College, with Dr Nauman, Dr Raza, Dr Mehwish and Dr Samreen serving as facilitators. The academic session examined the importance of fluoride in maintaining oral health and its role in the prevention and control of dental caries, one of the most common oral health problems affecting communities worldwide. The training placed preventive care alongside conventional clinical treatment, reinforcing the role of dentists in preventing oral disease, promoting healthy behaviours and educating individuals and communities about measures that can support long-term oral health. Understanding fluoride's role in protecting teeth During the workshop, Prof Dr Asghar Ali Shigri delivered an informative and interactive session explaining the mechanism of action of fluoride and its contribution to improving the resistance of tooth enamel against acid attacks. Students were introduced to the indications and benefits of topical fluoride therapy, with particular attention to fluoride gel application. The discussion connected the scientific principles of fluoride with its practical application, helping students understand the rationale behind professional topical fluoride use as part of a broader preventive dentistry approach. From classroom learning to clinical application A detailed demonstration gave students practical insight into the steps involved in fluoride gel application. The procedure covered patient preparation, selection and placement of appropriate trays, proper isolation and moisture control, application of fluoride gel, and precautions before, during and after the procedure. The facilitators emphasised the importance of following appropriate techniques and safety measures to support effective and suitable fluoride delivery. The practical component allowed students to observe the clinical application of concepts discussed during the workshop, strengthening the connection between theoretical knowledge and preventive dental practice. Preventive dentistry extends beyond disease treatment The facilitators also highlighted the importance of preventive dentistry in reducing the burden of oral diseases within the community. Students were encouraged to recognise that the role of dental professionals extends beyond treating established disease. Patient education, oral health promotion and appropriate preventive interventions are also important components of dental practice. This perspective is particularly relevant to dental caries, where prevention and risk reduction can complement treatment and help individuals maintain better oral health over time. Building skills for prevention-focused dental practice The interactive format encouraged students to actively participate in discussions and ask questions about fluoride therapy and its clinical application. The workshop further emphasised the importance of incorporating preventive strategies into routine dental practice. Fluoride gel application was discussed as a professional preventive measure when appropriately indicated, including for individuals who may have an increased risk of developing dental caries. The combination of academic discussion and practical demonstration gave students an opportunity to better understand how preventive concepts translate into clinical practice. Strengthening community dentistry education The workshop reflected the Department of Community Dentistry at Baqai Dental College's commitment to combining theoretical instruction with practical exposure and community-oriented preventive healthcare. Under the supervision of Prof Dr Asghar Ali Shigri and with the facilitation of Dr Nauman, Dr Raza, Dr Mehwish and Dr Samreen, the session brought together fluoride science, clinical technique and the broader principles of oral health promotion. By familiarising students with topical fluoride therapy and its preventive rationale, the workshop contributed to their academic and professional preparation for dentistry that places greater emphasis on disease prevention, patient education and community oral health. Ultimately, the training reinforced an important principle of preventive dentistry: effective oral healthcare is not limited to treating disease after it develops; prevention and education are fundamental to protecting long-term oral health. headline: CodeCoin Announces Official Approval of Stablecoin License at 2026 AFD, Marking Another Milestone in Its Global Payment Infrastructure Expansion
snippet: ASTANA, Kazakhstan , Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The global payment technology company CodeCoin made its debut at Astana Finance Days 2026. The founder, Benny, announced that CodeCoin had obtained the AFSA stablecoin issuance license. During the event, CodeCoin signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Al tyn Bank, and representatives from institutions such as Mastercard, Citibank, and China International Capital Corporation witnessed the signing. The digital currency issuance license marks an important step in CodeCoin's global compliance strategy. Benny said the company has placed compliance and real payment needs at the center of its approach from the outset. CodeCoin aims to combine regulatory authorization, established financial infrastructure and payment technology to address persistent challenges in cross-border payments, including cost, timeliness, transparency and availability. The company plans to advance relevant operations within Kazakhstan's regulatory framework while incorporating risk management, fund security and transaction traceability into its products and operations. In his address, Benny said businesses operating across borders can still face long settlement cycles, multiple intermediaries, restricted service hours and limited visibility into the status of funds. CodeCoin's product focus is to move money more safely, efficiently and predictably within a compliant framework, using clearer payment routes and transaction records to support international trade, supplier payments, corporate settlement and multi-currency treasury needs. CodeCoin positions itself as a provider of multi-currency payment infrastructure for businesses and individuals worldwide. Its services target corporate, merchant and cross-border remittance cases, with the goal of simplifying cross-border settlement, reducing foreign-exchange and intermediary friction, and provid ing more flexible payment paths for markets with insufficient coverage by traditional finance. The company plans to use regulatory authorization and financial-institution partnerships as the basis for payment products that enterprises can use in daily business. Security and risk management are also central to CodeCoin's public positioning. The company says its information security management system achieved ISO/IEC 27001 certification in April 2026. It also incorporates fund segregation, auditable payment processes, traceable transaction records, compliance controls and anti-money-laundering frameworks into its operations. CodeCoin's approach is that speed, transparency and regulatory alignment must develop together to support sustainable global payment services. CodeCoin is also exploring payment requirements for an AI-agent economy. Benny said that as AI agents become able to execute tasks, call services and complete commercial transactions, payment permissions, digital identity, accountability and transaction records will become essential infrastructure. AI agents should operate within company-defined spending limits, approved counterparties, time windows and authorization rules, with every payment linked to a clear identity and audit trail. "The real issue isn't trusting the software; it's about who takes the blame. The company is always responsible, never the code," he said. Hong Kong is CodeCoin's operating base and headquarters. The company is developing compliance and business networks across markets through banking partners, corporate clients, merchants and payment corridors. Systems previously built and operated by members of its management team reached more than 70 countries and served over one billion users. Those figures describe the team's prior experience rather than CodeCoin's current direct market coverage. The company has also outlined a CodeCoin Card offering for its ecosystem with support for Visa, JCB and UnionPay networks. The Altyn Bank (Subsidiary Bank of China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited) MOU is an important step in deepening CodeCoin's local financial cooperation in Kazakhstan. The cooperation will draw on Altyn Bank (Subsidiary Bank of China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited)'s local banking network as the parties explore opportunities in fintech, cross-border payments, digital finance and related applications. Representatives from Mastercard, Citi, CICC and other AFD participants witnessed the signing, reflecting industry attention to regional finance and cross-border payment connectivity. Kazakhstan occupies an important position connecting China, Central Asia and European markets. CodeCoin has already developed cooperation in the country. Its official news center reports that in June 2026 the company signed a strategic cooperation MOU with the Alatau City Authority State Fund to support cross-border digital payment infrastructure linking the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and Central Asia. The digital currency issuance license and latest banking cooperation strengthen the company's pivotal role in the international strategy of Kazakhstan . Going forward, CodeCoin plans to build around compliance and cross-border payments while developing products and partnerships in corporate payments, international trade settlement, AI-agent payments and multi-currency fund movement. headline: Williamson, Grace awarded WFNL best and fairest
snippet: Ararat’s Tom Williamson and Horsham Saints’ Ashlee Grace took out the Wimmera Football Netball League’s highest individual honours at the league’s 2026 vote count and presentation night on Monday September 15. Williamson was awarded the Toohey Medal after winning the senior football best and fairest. Grace claimed her third straight Hatcher Medal as the best and fairest player in A grade netball. In the senior football vote count, Williamson finished with 21 votes, beating out teammate and 2025 Toohey Medallist Ben Taylor, who finished runner up with 19 votes. The win marks Williamson's second senior best and fairest award, after claiming the 2024 Toohey Medal. Stawell's Josh Fowkes finished third with 18 votes, while Matty Lloyd and Reid Kuller rounded out the top five with 17 and 15 votes, respectively. Nhill's Tom Wheaton was awarded the best under 21 player, while Stawell forward Paul Summers was the leading goal-kicker, tallying 63 goals in the home and away season. In the A grade netball vote count, Grace finished with 33 votes, just beating out Dimboola defender Stephanie Glover, who was runner up with 32 votes. Horsham's Georgie Carberry finished third with 26 votes, while Horsham Saints teammates Jorja Clode (21 votes) and Maddison Bethune (17 votes) rounded out the top five. Clode was awarded for a great season in the goal circle, named the best under 21 player and leading goal shooter, with 945 goals. Speaking after receiving the Hatcher Medal, Grace credited the win to being part of a great team. "You never come into these things expecting to win and being in such a good team, such a consistent team, and being undefeated, everyone plays their part every week," she said. "You don't expect to get the votes in the end, you just do what you need for the team, and I suppose the umpires pay the credit where it's due." After an undefeated 2025 season, the Saints have continued their dominance in 2026 as they look to defend last year's premiership. Grace praised coach Vernetta Taylor as an integral part of their ongoing improvement. "Vernetta definitely challenges us, which is what we need and how we keep being successful," Grace said. "As we get older and more experienced, if you don't get pushed, then what's the point of being there as well? "So I know players like Megs, Shannon, Zeena and myself, as the older group of players, we definitely enjoy the encouragement and the push and the drive to keep getting better and it's showing in the game style that we're playing." In the women's senior football vote count, Natimuk United's Emma Van Egmond took out the best and fairest award, polling seven votes from just three games played. Laharum's Violet McGennisken was runner up with six votes. In the reserves football, Ararat's Alan Batchelor won back-to-back Hank Neil Medals, winning the best and fairest vote count with 22 votes. Nhill's Timothy Bone was awarded runner up, polling 16 votes, while Stawell's Kyan Mellor (15 votes), Ararat's Lewis Hodgins (14 votes) and Horsham's Jeremy Kemp (14 votes ) rounded out the top five. Ararat's Tash Noble was awarded the B grade netball best and fairest, polling 29 votes. Abby Hallam (Horsham Saints) was runner up with 27 votes and was also the leading goal shooter with 700 goals across the season. Jessica Cannane (Horsham Saints), Holly Graveson (Stawell) and Lucinda Taylor (Warrack Eagles) all finished equal third with 20 votes each. In C grade netball, a close vote count saw Nhill's Aroha McKinnon and Southern Mallee Thunder's Chantelle Fisher both poll 20 votes to share the best and fairest award. Horsham Saints' Sheridan Jones was runner up with 19 votes, followed by teammate Ayva Robertson with 17 votes. With 361 goals in the home and away season, Horsham's Georgie Hobbs was the leading goal shooter. Warrack Eagles' Deborah Templeton was the runaway winner in the C reserve netball, finishing with 27 votes, nine ahead of runner up Cassie Dunlop (Horsham Saints, 18 votes). Stawell's Michelle Beaton finished third with 15 votes and finished as leading goal shooter with 359. Following a strong home and away season across both football and netball, Horsham Saints were awarded the club championship for the 2026 season. Billie Schilling (Dimboola), Jemma Clarkson (Stawell) and Tom Eckel (Stawell) were also inducted as WFNL life members.
